Camera lane first. Make it immediate. Low fear. Low ceremony. Just go.
Open the camera or upload a quick clip. In this build, the 30-second stand-up lane actually records, hard-stops, previews, and posts to the local market.
Why this works: the bag removes face-pressure. The 30-second cap removes perfection pressure. Together, they make it easier to take the swing.

Load Up

This is the build lane. Capture a thought, shape a joke, stack a bit, organize an act, or order a set.

CLIP

One quick unit. A thought. A premise. A quick hit.

JOKE

Single hit, punch line, caption, setup, or answer.

BIT

Several jokes with shape and a point of view forming.

ACT

Bits grouped into a stronger lane with identity and momentum.

Conversations

Riffs, prompt drops, premise swings, comment chains, and testing lanes. For now this shows your local market feed from this browser.

Your Bag

The bag is identity without face pressure. It gives you a lane without demanding your real one.

What’s the bag? It lets you be who you want. Nobody cares what you look like. Nobody cares where you’re from. If you’re funny, you’re funny. That’s the permission slip.

Comic Strip Lab

Not forgotten. Not buried. This is the second creative engine: fixed-world panel comedy, stick-figure logic, dialogue, pacing, and visual joke construction.

Three-panel starter

Use the strip like a joke machine: setup, tilt, hit. Keep it simple first.

PANEL 1
Setup. Who’s here? What’s the situation?
PANEL 2
Complication. Twist the assumption a little.
PANEL 3
Hit. Pay it off fast.

Why this lane matters

Visual joke engine

Good for ideas that want structure but not stage presence.

Character world

Lets recurring characters and archetypes build over time.

Low-pressure writing

Useful bridge between a thought and a performed bit.

Shared rendering system

Eventually this becomes fixed templates, bubbles, and stick-figure world rules.
